q: What OSHA standard covers powered industrial trucks (forklifts)?
mnemonic: 178 = PIT. Think '1-7-8 wheels on a truck.'

q: What is the most common type of forklift accident?
mnemonic: TIP = most common. A forklift is top-heavy by design.

q: Material handling accounts for approximately what % of the cost of doing business?
mnemonic: HALF the cost of business is just moving stuff around.

q: What is a counterbalanced forklift?
choices: A truck with forks on all four sides
A truck with forks at the front and a counterweight in the rear
A truck balanced by hydraulic leveling
A truck with adjustable axle weight
mnemonic: Front = forks. Back = fat counterweight. Like a seesaw.

q: The three major parts of a forklift are:
mnemonic: BOH: Body, Overhead guard, Hydraulic lift.

q: If you know how to drive a car, you also know how to drive a forklift.
mnemonic: REAR steer, different controls, different physics. Car ≠ forklift.

q: All forklift controls and gauges are the same across models.
mnemonic: Every manufacturer is different. Always learn YOUR truck.

q: When traveling with a load on a level surface, forks should be raised approximately:
choices: As high as possible for visibility
mnemonic: 4-6 inches = about a hand's width. Low for stability, high enough to clear bumps.

q: Loads should be carried with the mast tilted to which position?
mnemonic: BACK it up. Tilt mast BACK to cradle the load against the carriage.

q: When traveling on a ramp with a load, the load should always point:
mnemonic: Load goes HIGH. Up ramp = forward. Down ramp = reverse.

q: The load center is measured from:
choices: The rear axle to center of load
The front face of the forks to the center of gravity of the load
The mast to the tip of the forks
The overhead guard to the load
mnemonic: Face of Forks to CG. Standard = 24 inches.

q: The front wheels of a forklift serve as the ___ between truck weight and load weight.
mnemonic: FULCRUM = seesaw pivot. Front axle is the pivot point.

q: Rear-end steering on a forklift causes:
choices: Tighter turning radius than a car
The rear end to swing to the outside of the turn
Both front and rear to track the same path
The front end to swing wide
mnemonic: TAIL SWINGS OUT. Watch your rear end around corners and pedestrians.

q: When is it OK to give someone a ride on a forklift?
choices: When they need a quick lift to a mezzanine
When riding on the forks with a safety platform
mnemonic: NEVER. No passengers. Period.

q: If a forklift starts to tip over sideways, the operator should:
choices: Stay in, grip wheel, brace with feet, lean away
Try to steer out of the tip
mnemonic: STAY and BRACE. Jumping puts you UNDER 9,000 lbs of steel.

q: Who always has the right of way?
choices: Pedestrians always have right of way
It depends on the workplace rules
mnemonic: PEOPLE FIRST. Always. No exceptions.

q: At what speed should a forklift be driven?
choices: A speed consistent with load and conditions
mnemonic: No fixed MPH. Match speed to load, surface, visibility, and traffic.

q: Why sound the horn with several short blasts?
choices: Short blasts attract more attention than one long blast
To test the horn each time
mnemonic: SHORT = SHARP attention. One long drone gets tuned out.

q: How should fork width be set for a loaded pallet?
choices: As narrow as possible for precision
Spread for equal weight on each fork arm
Width doesn't matter if capacity isn't exceeded
mnemonic: EQUAL weight, WIDE spread. Balance the load across both forks.

q: When must a pre-operation inspection be completed?
choices: Daily / at the beginning of every shift
Only when the truck looks damaged
mnemonic: EVERY SHIFT, EVERY DAY. 24/7 ops = inspect at each shift change.

q: Can you operate a forklift if the data plate is missing or unreadable?
choices: Yes, if you know the capacity from memory
mnemonic: NO PLATE = NO GO. Capacity must be readable on the truck.

q: Is a forklift in good condition if some gauges are broken?
choices: Yes, if it still drives fine
mnemonic: ALL instruments must work. Broken gauge = out of service.

q: Which of these will take a forklift out of service?
choices: Leaking hydraulics, faulty brakes, steering problems, parking brake failure
Minor dent on the overhead guard
mnemonic: LBSP: Leaks, Brakes, Steering, Parking brake. Any one = shut it down.

q: A brake pedal that sinks to the floor under pressure is in good operating condition.
mnemonic: SINKING = FAILING. Floor pedal means brake system failure.

q: Where do you find the load capacity of a forklift?
mnemonic: DATA PLATE. Mounted on the truck. Shows capacity at specific load center.

q: What should be done with a defective or unsafe forklift?
choices: Use it carefully until end of shift
Inform supervisor immediately and take out of service
Note it in the logbook for next shift
mnemonic: REPORT + REMOVE. Tag it, park it, tell your supervisor. NOW.

q: What is the main purpose of the overhead guard?
mnemonic: FALLING STUFF. Boxes, debris from shelves above. Not rated for full loads.

q: The most important safety device on a forklift is:
mnemonic: YOU. No safety device replaces a trained, alert operator.

q: Can you place hands and feet outside the operator compartment if head and body are inside?
mnemonic: ALL body parts stay INSIDE. Hands, feet, everything.

q: Before driving into a trailer at a dock, what must you check?
choices: Only that the trailer is present
Trailer can handle weight, wheel chocks in place, dock plate secure
That the trailer driver has left the cab
The color coding of the loading bay
mnemonic: WCD: Weight capacity, Chocks, Dock plate. All three.

q: If a load appears unsafely stacked and might collapse, you should:
choices: Try to restack it from the forklift
Leave it alone, cordon the area, inform supervisor
Push it to a safer spot
mnemonic: LEAVE + CORDON + REPORT. Don't be a hero with a collapsing load.

q: Who is responsible for preventing workplace accidents?
mnemonic: EVERYONE. Safety is universal responsibility.

q: When leaving a forklift, what should you do with the key?
choices: Leave it in for the next operator
mnemonic: OFF + OUT. Prevents unauthorized use.

q: How often must forklift operators be re-evaluated?
mnemonic: 3 YEARS. But sooner if accident, near-miss, or unsafe driving observed.

q: OSHA requires which 3 components for forklift training?
choices: Written test, road test, physical exam
mnemonic: FPE: Formal instruction, Practical training, Evaluation. Learn, Do, Prove.

q: If trained on a sit-down counterbalanced truck, are you qualified for a stand-up reach truck?
mnemonic: Different TYPE = different training. Each truck type needs its own cert.

q: Must employers retain forklift certification records?
choices: Yes, copies of certs, tests, and evaluations
mnemonic: PAPER TRAIL. Certs + tests + evals. Keep them on file.

q: What triggers mandatory retraining before the 3-year cycle?
choices: Accident, near-miss, unsafe operation observed, or new truck type
mnemonic: CANE: Crash, Almost-crash, Negligent driving, Equipment change.

q: When refueling a gas/diesel forklift, should the engine be running?
choices: No, never leave engine running while refueling
mnemonic: ENGINE OFF. Always. No exceptions when fueling.

q: What PPE is needed when charging/replacing an electric forklift battery?
choices: Protective gloves, eye/face protection, acid-resistant apron
mnemonic: GEA: Gloves, Eyes, Apron. Battery acid = sulfuric acid burns.

q: Is it OK to quick-charge an electric forklift battery during lunch?
choices: No, partial charges can damage the battery
mnemonic: FULL CHARGE ONLY. Partial cycles damage battery cells.

q: Wide and long loads are more unstable than other types of loads.
mnemonic: TRUE. Big loads shift CG and increase tip-over risk.

q: If the hydraulic lift mechanism fails, should you try to repair it yourself?
choices: Yes, if you have basic tools
No, only qualified maintenance personnel should repair it
Yes, if it's a simple hose
mnemonic: NOT YOUR JOB. Hydraulics = qualified mechanic only.

q: On machine decals, which signal word indicates the greatest level of concern?
mnemonic: DANGER > Warning > Caution > Notice. D is for DEADLY serious.

q: Adequate forklift training prevents what percentage of forklift accidents?
mnemonic: MOST accidents are preventable with proper training. Way more than 10%.

q: How many classes of powered industrial trucks does OSHA define?
mnemonic: SEVEN classes. 7 like the days of the week.

q: What are the two power sources for powered industrial trucks?
choices: Electric battery and internal combustion engine
mnemonic: Two sources: ELECTRIC battery or ICE (internal combustion engine). That is it.

q: Trucks with pneumatic tires are typically designed for what environment?
mnemonic: PNEUMATIC = OUTSIDE. Air-filled tires handle rough terrain.

q: Trucks with cushion tires are typically designed for what environment?
mnemonic: CUSHION = INSIDE. Smooth solid rubber for smooth warehouse floors.

q: A powered industrial truck should only be used to carry:
mnemonic: MATERIALS ONLY. Never people, never other vehicles.

q: OSHA requires all PIT operators to complete what types of training?
mnemonic: FORMAL (classroom) + PRACTICAL (hands-on). Both required.

q: As a PIT operator, you must be aware of environments where you should:
choices: Drive faster to reduce exposure time
mnemonic: Some environments are OFF LIMITS. Know where NOT to operate (flammable areas, confined spaces, etc).

q: Which OSHA class includes electric motor rider trucks with cushion tires?
mnemonic: Class I = Electric motor rider trucks. Think I = Indoor electric.

q: Which OSHA class covers internal combustion engine trucks with cushion tires?
mnemonic: Class IV = IC engine, cushion tires. 4 = Four cushion corners inside.

q: Which OSHA class covers internal combustion engine trucks with pneumatic tires?
mnemonic: Class V = IC engine, pneumatic tires. V = Venture outside.

q: Electric-powered forklifts produce fewer emissions, making them better suited for:
mnemonic: Electric = no exhaust fumes = safe INDOORS. IC engines produce carbon monoxide.

q: Internal combustion forklifts should NOT be operated in:
mnemonic: IC engines = carbon monoxide. NO enclosed/unventilated areas. You will die.

q: Which OSHA class includes electric motor narrow aisle trucks?
mnemonic: Class II = Electric narrow aisle. II = two narrow aisles.

q: Which OSHA class includes electric motor hand trucks (pallet jacks)?
mnemonic: Class III = electric hand trucks/walkies. III = 3 letters in "hand" minus 1... just memorize III = hand trucks.

q: What dangerous gas can internal combustion forklifts produce?
mnemonic: CO = Carbon Monoxide = silent killer. IC engines in enclosed spaces = death.
